_comment: Personal Claude Code settings for Pol4720 — copy to ~/.claude/settings.json.
This is a STARTING POINT, not a snapshot: the account currently runs the Claude
Code defaults. Everything here is opt-in; delete what you do not want.
JSON has no comment syntax, so the underscore-prefixed keys carry the notes.
Claude Code ignores unknown keys, but keep them tidy anyway.
NEVER put an API key, token or password in any of these files. They are committed.
_comment_permissions: Read-only commands pre-approved so routine work does not stop for a prompt.
Nothing here can modify the working tree, the remote, or anything outside it.
The `deny` list is the important half: it blocks destructive and history-rewriting
operations even when a permission mode would otherwise allow them.
_comment_env: Environment variables for every session. Values only — never secrets.
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE keeps __pycache__ out of the working tree during audits,
so `git status` stays readable while Claude is running scripts.
_comment_hooks: Hooks are commands the HARNESS runs at lifecycle points — Claude cannot be asked to
remember to do them, which is precisely why they exist. See docs and the
`update-config` skill for the full event list and the JSON each event receives.
None are enabled by default here. The two below are commented-out examples of the
hooks most worth having; move them into a real `hooks` key to activate.
PostToolUse on Edit|Write  -> run the formatter on the file that changed
PreToolUse  on Bash        -> block a command pattern before it runs
Stop                       -> warn about uncommitted work at the end of a turn

hooks.command: if [ "${CLAUDE_FILE_PATH##*.}" = "py" ]; then ruff format "$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
